messages:
sophie: FYI — Tier-1 bank POC asking about an on-prem, air-gapped install. their two big asks: 1) keep BOM tiny (customer will move bundles via USB/sneakernet) and 2) ability to deliver urgent security hotpatches between full upgrade windows. also they want to plug into their HSM for key signing. what are our options / constraints?

mike: short answer: yes, but tradeoffs. we support immutable signed bundles + delta patch bundles for runtime and small packages. model artifacts (large .bin/.safetensors) typically require full bundle replace unless you ship a model-diff flow (we don't widely support model binary diffs today).

sophie: ok. they specifically asked whether we can ship a small "security-only" delta that patches system libs + runtime CVEs without changing models. is that feasible?

anita: feasible for the runtime and our controllers. we can generate signed patch bundles that contain only /opt/redwood/runtime/* and agent binaries. verification flow: deploy-device runs a local signature check (HSM or software keystore) before applying. example verify command we run on-device: ```
redwood-offline apply --bundle /media/usb/patch-2026-03-01.tar.gz --verify --pubkey /etc/redwood/keys/pub.pem
```

mike: couple of caveats: 1) delta bundles must be built against the exact bundle-version baseline installed on the device (we compute checksums at build time). 2) if a runtime patch changes KV-cache format or model-serving kernel ABI, you may need a short restart and potential token cache flush. we flag ABI changes in the bundle manifest.

sophie: HSM question — can the customer sign bundles with their HSM and we still verify?

anita: yes — we support external signing. two modes: customer signs everything with their HSM and we accept that public key in the device truststore, or we act as the signer and provide signed deltas that the customer validates with their HSM. either way, trust anchor is a cert fingerprint stored in /etc/redwood/trust-roots.

james: pricing/ops side: hotpatching as an SLA feature is an add-on. for POC we can include 2 emergency patches in 90-day trial at no charge; for production we'd include options: ad-hoc hotpatches billed per-patch + optional on-call engineering support. rough tier: $2k per emergency patch + $250/hr for ops support outside normal SLA, or a bundled plan (eg $15k/quarter for up to 10 patches + priority 24/7 escalation). final pricing depends on contract.

sophie: the customer also asked about upgrade cadence recommendations so they can plan change windows. what do we recommend?

anita: recommended ops cadence: - Major feature/QA upgrade: quarterly (planned) - Security-only deltas: ad-hoc (emergency) but grouped into monthly cumulative deltas when possible to reduce churn - End-to-end acceptance test period: we recommend 48h soak in staging before any full bundle apply in prod. Note: model updates are separate — unless model weights change, you won't need a full runtime bundle.

mike: operational constraints to call out to customer: 1) offline devices must have a small bootstrap agent that can accept signed bundles and perform atomic swap (we ship that). 2) we require recorded bundle fingerprints for chain-of-custody (they asked for audit). 3) if they want model diffs (patching only parts of a model file), that's R&D and will add time.

sophie: legal/security questionnaire item: they asked about SBOM and binary provenance. can we provide per-bundle SBOM and signing metadata?

anita: yes. every bundle includes an sbom.json and a manifest.json with: checksums, signer identity, build-timestamp, and CVE tags. we can redact internal build metadata for customer-facing artifacts if needed.

deploy-bot: [auto] created doc: https://internal.redwood/docs/offline-bundles/runbook — runbook + sample manifests. (visibility: sales + eng-ops)

james: next steps proposed: 1) draft a POC SOW addendum that includes: a) two hotpatches during POC, b) external HSM signing integration test, c) bundle verification runbook handoff. 2) present pricing options (ad-hoc vs retainer). 3) schedule a 60-min technical run-through with their infra team next week.

sophie: thanks. I'm drafting the SOW now. @mike @anita can you validate the HSM flow and the sample verify command? I'd like to have a one-pager to send the customer before the call.

mike: will validate the verify flow and add a short comment about ABI-change flags in the manifest.

anita: I'll prep a minimal KB snippet and an example sbom.json redaction example. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sophie: perfect. i'll send the one-pager and attach the POC SOW draft. calling out dependencies: customer needs a jumpbox to load bundles, one admin with ability to update truststore, and a maintenance window for any runtime restarts.

james: i'll price the three commercial options and add a note that rapid-response hotpatch coverage requires a signed SOW and dedicated on-call rotation.

sophie: great — closing the loop here. follow-ups once we have the draft SOW + KB. :thumbsup:
